audit_findings.title: Acquisition-dependent growth may be credited without its capital cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Future acquisition spending would be a reinvestment requirement supporting projected OE growth but is excluded from ordinary owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition of businesses that complement or expand our operations has been and continues to be an important element of our business strategy.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition strategy is documented, but the record does not demonstrate that the modeled 3%-6% growth requires future acquisitions. FY2026 sales excluding VACCO grew 9.2%, and computed first-quarter growth excluding VACCO was approximately 11.5%, both above the modeled rates. Acquisition dependence therefore remains a forward-looking risk rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Track organic revenue, margin, and OE growth separately from acquired contributions; rerun growth or include normalized acquisition reinvestment if organic performance cannot support the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 owner earnings do not represent the full current VACCO perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2026 OE anchor includes only the post-July 18, 2025 portion of VACCO, while shares and the balance-sheet bridge reflect the consolidated current perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 18, 2025, the Company acquired the issued and outstanding capital stock of VACCO from ESCO Technologies Inc. for $ 276.7 .
audit_findings.explanation: The temporal mismatch is demonstrated: FY2026 included $83.9 million of VACCO sales, while the first full post-acquisition quarter included $33.3 million. The missing annual OE contribution cannot be established because standalone VACCO profit, capital expenditure, taxes, and working-capital requirements are not supplied. The likely direction is upward, but materiality to value remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Construct full-year pro forma VACCO OE using filed or acquired-business statements, including recurring capital expenditure, working capital, taxes, interest, and only realized synergies, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Treatment of acquisition and restructuring charges is undocumented
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.0 million pretax in FY2026: $14.8 million of acquisition-related and purchase-accounting effects plus $6.2 million of restructuring charges
audit_findings.mechanism: Improperly retaining nonrecurring charges depresses anchor OE; improperly removing recurring restructuring costs inflates anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The net income attributable to common stockholders of $287.6 in fiscal 2026 was impacted by $14.8 of acquisition and related costs, $6.2 of restructuring and consolidation charges, $49.8 of interest expense, and $81.7 of income tax expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosure gap is demonstrated because the $248.7 million anchor is not reconciled to the filed charges. The gross identified exposure equals 8.4% of anchor OE, but the actual adjustment is unknown because $13.2 million of the acquisition-related amount was a purchase-accounting charge and the cash, tax, add-back, and recurrence treatment is not shown.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $248.7 million anchor line by line, identifying cash versus noncash purchase-accounting effects, tax impacts, amounts already captured through D&A or working capital, and evidence supporting any nonrecurring classification.

audit_findings.title: The retained interest expense may not reflect the now-unhedged financing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.1 million first-quarter FY2027 net interest expense; $40.4 million annualized versus $49.8 million in FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest remains inside equity-level OE, so differences between historical and current financing costs change the OE anchor directly.
audit_findings.evidence: During the three-year period prior to December 30, 2025, we utilized the Interest Rate Swap to fix a portion of the variable rate interest expense associated with the Term Loan, but the Company does not have an interest rate swap in place as of the date of this Annual Report.
audit_findings.explanation: The first fully post-expiry quarter does not demonstrate an omitted financing burden: annualized net interest was $9.4 million below FY2026, while total debt fell from $875.5 million to $806.2 million and a further $50.0 million term-loan repayment was filed. The available current evidence therefore indicates that mechanically retaining FY2026 interest would modestly understate value, not overstate it; the scale is only 3.8% of the $248.7 million anchor before tax and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Complete a debt-by-debt interest recast using the $46.0 million post-quarter term-loan balance, $200.0 million revolver, fixed-rate notes, contractual spreads, current benchmark rates, cash interest income, and scheduled refinancing.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease reinvestment may bypass the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.2 million FY2026 finance-lease cash payments, comprising $4.6 million principal and $1.6 million interest
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease amortization is added back to OE without deducting leased-asset additions or equivalent principal, recurring capital consumption is omitted.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash paid associated with finance lease liabilities was $ 6.2 and $ 6.0 for the fiscal years ended March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification should be reconciled, but even the entire $6.2 million payment equals only 2.5% of the $248.7 million OE anchor. The filed $1.6 million interest is already within earnings, while the potentially omitted principal is $4.6 million; neither amount is large enough to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $5.4 million finance-lease asset amortization, $1.5 million of new finance-lease assets, and $4.6 million principal through the OE calculation and deduct the appropriate recurring reinvestment exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Cross-currency swap liability may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.7 million latest filed liability, equal to approximately $0.21 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: If not offset by the hedged foreign net investment or already reflected in cash, the derivative liability should reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of the Cross Currency Swap was a liability of $ 7.7 and $ 0.2 at March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, respectively, and was measured using Level 2 inputs.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q updates the liability from $7.7 million to $6.7 million. A full standalone deduction would reduce the $3,083-$4,247 million scenario equity values by only 0.16%-0.22%, or about $0.21 per share, and cannot change the valuation conclusion. Whether any deduction is conceptually appropriate still depends on avoiding double-counting the offsetting currency exposure.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 27, 2026 settlement value, maturity cash mechanics, and treatment of the hedged Schaublin net investment; if no offset is already represented, deduct $6.7 million from the bridge and rerun per-share values.
